newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA CONFIDENT DURING IMF ASSESSMENT TALKS (RPT).
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA CONFIDENT DURING IMF ASSESSMENT TALKS (RPT).

text.p: Romania's centrist government expressed confidence on Wednesday that it would win IMF approval of its progress in introducing reforms at the outset of talks on securing fresh tranches of Fund credits.

"During the meeting a short evaluation was made of the implementation of the programme agreed with the the IMF," a government statement said after talks got under way with the IMF's chief negotiator for Romania, Poul Thomsen.
"It stressed the fact that Romania's fiscal and monetary policies have allowed it to achieve macro-economic stability."
Thomsen, who arrived on Tuesday a week after an IMF technical team began its assessment, refused to comment.

After the IMF team passes judgment on progress made since the government reform programme was launched in February, its Board in Washington will meet next month to decide on releasing a second tranche of around $86 million.
The disbursement will be the second of five under a 13-month stand-by accord worth a total $430 million.

Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea said this month his government had met many objectives stipulated by the IMF, including a stable currency, a fall in the inflation rate to 2.3 percent in June from more than 30 percent in March and control of the budget deficit.
He said there was "no risk whatsoever" of the IMF postponing further disbursements.

Romania's centrist government, elected last November after seven years of rule by leftists, has pledged to cut the current account deficit to $1.4 billion from last year's $2.3 billion, increase foreign exchange reserves, speed up privatisation and privatise at least one bank.
A second IMF review is due early in 1998.
The Fund suspended credits last year, saying the leftist government of the time had overspent and hobbled foreign exchange markets ahead of the election it eventually lost.
